statements.status_notes: CVE-2025-69277: crypto_core_ed25519_is_valid_point() in libsodium could accept points outside the main prime-order subgroup, because the subgroup check only tested X == 0 (https://00f.net/2025/12/30/libsodium-vulnerability/). Upstream fixed it in commit ad3004e, which also requires Y == Z in ge25519_is_on_main_subgroup() (https://github.com/jedisct1/libsodium/commit/ad3004ec8731730e93fcfbbc824e67eadc1c1bae); Debian shipped the same fix as DSA-6094-1 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2025-69277). Alpine 3.23 carries that commit as core_ed25519_is_valid_point.patch in libsodium 1.0.20-r1 and lists CVE-2025-69277 under 1.0.20-r1 in its secfixes (https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/3.23-stable/main/libsodium/APKBUILD). The only libsodium build published for Alpine 3.23, on x86_64 and aarch64, is 1.0.20-r1, built from that APKBUILD with the patch applied, so every published build carries the fix and 1.0.20-r1 is the lowest published version.
